text.p: Following are the main stories in Monday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Government has directed Indah Water consortium to exempt religious schools, Chinese independent schools and premises occupied by some non-governmental organisations from paying sewerage charges, said Housing and Local Government Minister Ting Chew Peh. Water services utility Indah Water is a subsidiary of Prime Utilities Bhd.
- The nine-day Langkawi International Motor Show 1996 ended on Sunday with exhibitors clinching sales worth hundreds of millions of ringgit, said organiser Le Proton Exhibition Servies.
- Three state executive councillors of Kelantan who are members of Prime Minister Mohamad's party have left their political posts in the opposition-ruled northern state.
- New car maker United Shelby Sdn Bhd plans to produce one of America's classic supercars, the Shelby, at a 338 million ringgit Malaysian plant, company officials said.
- Hotels managed to record an average occupancy rate of 85 percent this year despite greater competition, and tariffs rose by an average 14 percent.
